answer: Identity Accumulation Penalty. Each new address controlled by an operator incurs a cumulative cost tied to their existing on-chain fable of activity, where past legitimate behavior determines future registration burdens. The karst formation of reputation slowly builds barriers that resist rapid sybilization, forcing attackers to either preserve authentic history or abandon prior gains. A glacier-like delay prevents instant mass creation—each identity after the first costs exponentially more in delayed transaction fees and reputational collateral.
